habitat_notes: slightly turbid shallow fringing reef. high LC. few predators and few scarids
slightly turbid shallow fringing reef. high LC, high numbers of Pomacentrids, lethrinids relatively common
reef slope - lots of lethrinids, some lutjanids and carangids
reef slope - Cetoscarus male, female and juvenile
Moderate relief and high diversity corals, high diversity fish but low numbers food fish
Moderate relief and high diversity corals, high diversity fish but low numbers food fish; some turbidity
Complex reef w high biodiversity, some turbidity
Complex reef w high biodiversity, high turbidity
Ilili Inner patch reef very damaged - looks like dynamite and storm damage - large broken pieces of coral
Ilili Inner patch reef, some damaged corals, also large vase like corals and echinoderms and molluscs
Matenga Inner patch reef, old dynamite damage - big pieces, dead staghorn abundant, isolated patches of coral; good coral in shallows w schools of Poms
Matenga Inner patch reef, banks of Galaxea, many soft corals, few fish
Outer reef slope near Songa, Mod-Low relief, good HC growth, moderate fish diversity
Outer reef slope near Songa, Low relief, good HC growth, moderate fish diversity

Site near sandy beach in town, Black rocky coastline, reef about 500m from shore – inner reef of rock boulders covered with corals, further out reef formed and some rock substrate, lots sand.Slopes at 50 degrees.

Site near sandy beach in town, Black rocky coastline, reef about 500m from shore – inner reef of rock boulders covered with corals, further out reef formed and some rock substrate, lots sand.Slopes at 50 degrees.
Reef slope, moderate relief, very  clear water, large tabulate Acropora. Drops to over 30m.
Reef slope, moderate relief, very  clear water, large tabulate Acropora. Drops to over 30m.

Scattered corals growing on black larva near shore dropping quite steeply. Towards bay scattered coral reefs on sandy bottom, complex structure of spurs and separated reefs. Many Acropora plates dead with brown turf algae. Some COT.

Scattered corals growing on black larva near shore dropping quite steeply. Towards bay scattered coral reefs on sandy bottom, complex structure of spurs and separated reefs. Many Acropora plates dead with brown turf algae. Some COT.

Shore dive from rocky shore line with small sandy bay. Fringing reef with short spur and groove, drops to 15 -17 m at 30 degrees, viz. around 15m. COT outbreak. Counted >30. Most of the Acropora plates dead.
Fringing reef off rocks and small sandy bays on east side of Grande Comore.  Shore dive across very wide reef flat (500-1000m) to small reef dropping to around 11m.

Coral growing on larval rock off rocky shore; scattered corals but fairly diverse. High relief, moderately complex topography  and some low scattered patches of coral. Shelving to rock, sand and rubble.

Fringing reef off sandy beach on island called Mnaybadji Island(?). Dynamite damage clearly seen as extensive areas of rubble.  Coral bleaching beginning – many scattered small colonies are bleaching.
Deep platform reef offshore, starting at around 15-16m and sloping gently to 20 m. Low coral diversity, low relief.
Steep drop on sandy wall off Mea island on the east side. Patchy reef with a lot of sand but diverse corals and quite high relief.

Fringing reef off Moheli – South-west of the village. High coral cover and diversity – Porites, Acropora plates and Pocillopora, but lots of bleaching too. Some silt from run-off due to heavy rain so visibility down to 12m.
Patchy corals on sandy slope off mangroves. Very turbid.
Steep slope on sand about 100m from shore of seagrass, some mangrove and sand flat. Fairly turbid, rubble, high algal cover, soft corals, forams, ascidians and other benthic invertebrates.
Steep slope on sand about 100m from shore of seagrass, some mangrove and sand flat. Fairly turbid, rubble, high algal cover, soft corals, forams, ascidians and other benthic invertebrates.
Gentle slope, turbid conditions, with very low coral cover. Occasional coral outcrops, otherwise very low relief, bare rock, except at start of dive.
Fringing rocky algal reef sloping gently with high cover of algae, sponges and soft corals; some corals.

Complex high relief steep slope (70- 80 degrees) with channels; many encrusting corals (e.g. Montipora) and large sea fans; shelves up onto sandy bed with scattered coral heads. Relatively high coral cover. Lots of fishing line and old net.
Rocky reef fringing the raised coral island off the NW shore of the bay. Silty, with many soft corals and sponges including the large Zestospongia; strong current.

Rocky reef fringing the raised coral island off the NW shore of the bay further North than Loky 8. Rubble, bare rock with algae, notably red algae (probably Peyssonnelia), many soft corals, but with some high relief coral bommies; very silty.

Exposed reef with well developed spur and groove structure, ending at 17m, on silty sandy bed with very few isolated hard and soft corals heads. Large Acropora robusta  corals common. Low relief, many encrusting corals, algae and soft corals.
same reef edge as Vohemar 13 just slightly further south.
Similar to Loky 6.

Fringing reef on north side of Ankao Island, towards the entrance to Ankao Bay. Clear water, huge stands of Galaxea onto sand at around 6m. Ridge of corals and large expanses of sand. First reefs without a heavy silt load!

Back reef lagoon type habitat but with strong currents due to being the main S-N channel between two islands. Clear water, large scattered coral bommies with reasonable cover, dominated by Pocillopora
Outer reef edge off fringing reef from Ankao Island; a little turbid. Densely scattered large coral bommies with reasonably complex topography, low fish diversity but some groups abundant

The most developed and diverse coral community seen on the survey. Coral cover high also. In the shallows towards the reef flat (<7m) soft corals dominated. In places a red filamentous algae was very common – uncertain if this might be related to the large seaweed farm on Ankao Island.

Back reef lagoon type habitat but with strong currents due to being the main S-N channel between two islands. Clear water, large scattered coral bommies with reasonable cover, dominated by Pocillopora.
Leeward reef flat, 2-5m depth. Healthy corals scattered across sandy flat with expanses of rubble in places. Little bleaching observed; fairly high cover of old dead corals. 1 COT.
Leeward reef flat, 2-5m depth. Healthy corals scattered across sandy flat with expanses of rubble in places. Little bleaching observed; fairly high cover of old dead corals. 1 COT.

Steep 90 degree wall that drops to around 500m on the chart, from a reef top  of 12-15m. Wall with many sea fans and Tubastrea coral (see photo). Reef top a shelf at 11-16m depth with many soft corals, and small plate Acropora and other hard corals. Acropora and other hard corals.

Steep 90 degree wall that drops to around 500m on the chart, from a reef top  of 12-15m. Wall with many sea fans and Tubastrea coral (see photo). Reef top a shelf at 11-16m depth with many soft corals, and small plate Acropora and other hard corals. Acropora and other hard corals.
exposed fringing reef to Metundo island,extensive flat plateau at 8-10m. this is not Baixo Pinguim but only 1 tn so added to BP site as tn4
Extensive deep reef at 6-10m, S facing wall to shelf at 17m.

Outer reef slope of around 45 degrees to sand bottom at 13-16m, with fairly complex topography, scattered large massive corals, many soft corals and about 30% live coral cover. Above the slope a reef flat at around 5m depth largely bare of hard corals but many soft corals.

Outer reef slope of around 45 degrees to sand bottom at 13-16m, with fairly complex topography, scattered large massive corals, many soft corals and about 30% live coral cover. Above the slope a reef flat at around 5m depth largely bare of hard corals but many soft corals.
Turbid, high coral relief with some massive Pavona dropping onto sandy channels. Acropora stag horn coral very common in shallows.

Shallow extensive flat reef at 2-5m with very high live coral cover – largely Acropora branching corals, but also large Pavona. Impressive live coral cover – at least 80%. And very clear, about 18m visibility.

Shallow fringing reef on eastern more leeward side of sand cay, from 0.5 to 5m depth to sand bottom. Much dead coral and sea urchins common (Diadema setosum and Echinothrix diadema). Dead coral is Acropora plate and stag horn; likely bleaching damage and then collapsed. Live Acropora stag horn also common.

Southern exposure facing the strong SE seas. Submerged reef platform at 3-5 m of bare rock with a few scattered large coral formations, much algae especially reds. Reef then slopes at 45 degrees to sand bottom at 9-10m. Slope typified by large stands of Goniopora, some dead some alive. Few, small isolated patches of bleached corals. Moderate rugosity and coral diversity and spur formation.

Wide reef slope from small sand and coral cay exposed at low tide. Slopes gently at 20-30 degrees to sand at 13-15m. Low relief reef, much bare rock, dead coral and rubble; occasional live coral heads.

Narrow fringing reef off sand cay dropping to sand at around 10m. Much of reef dead and broken coral pieces or rubble – looks like Acropora plates and branching collapsed after death ie from bleaching. Some coral recruits of 5-10 years old -  Pocillopora, Acropora. Some large areas of live Acropora branching in 1-2 m, and some live Goniopora banks. Noticeably very little algae.
Reef plateau of rock, sand and algae at 5m, then drops at 90 deg to around 22m sand bottom. Wall bare with turf algae and reds, very few corals. Some coral heads on plateau.  wall is in the mlango;

Similar reef profile to Dindini 8 but more varied structure and live hard corals, also soft corals, with wall sloping at 70-80 degrees and bottom with mixed corals on sand.Very cold water cam flooding in from deep just before high tide. Apparently a cold upwelling from open sea (source: Abdullah the skipper).

Inner lagoonal reef off Chole Island within the protected Chole Bay.  Brilliantly clear water, high (6-10m) spurs of coral growing off a sand bottom at around 13-15m. Channels with rubble. Occasional small bleached Pocillopora. Millepora common in shallows.

As for Utumbi 13  - inner lagoonal reef of coral spurs and extensive coral patches on lagoonal sand bottom around 12m. Later tide and further in the bay brought more turbid water; some coral damage/rubble

Outer fringing reef off Chole island. Exposed to SE. reef flat, then crest followed by reef platform at around 3- 5m depth with channels. Platform largely bare rock with algae particularly Turbinaria and soft corals.This extends for about 100m from crest, then slopes steeply initially, then gently to rubble –sand bottom at around 20m. Many soft corals in shallow part of reef. Reef slope with a lot of dead coral, but occasional large live bommies and many young recruits. Moderate rugosity.

Just 300m south of Yuyuni 10 so similar reef structure and orientation. Outer fringing reef off Chole island. Exposed to SE. Reef flat then crest drops to reef platform at around 5m depth. This extends for about 100m, then drops steeply, 70 degrees, to about 12m, then drops more gently, 30 degrees, to rubble –sand bottom at around 20m; Very cold water came flooding in from deep just before high tide.

Marginal fringing reef facing west within the port channel. Few scattered corals on sandy slope of around 40 degrees. Reef largely detrital, viz reasonable (around 15m) but little hard substrate. Seagrass and sand between coral bommies.

Marginal fringing reef facing west within the port channel. Few scattered corals on sandy slope of around 40 degrees. Reef largely detrital, viz reasonable (around 15m) but little hard substrate. Seagrass and sand between coral bommies.
North facing fringing reef. Steep slope dominated by Plerogyra coral (bubble coral).
Huge banks of Galaxea, largely intact, some dead parts colonised by grey sponge.
Upper reef platform from 9-17m depth, complex and rugose w high coral cover & div. then drops at around 95 degrees from around 20m depth to 200m.

more exposed facing east, very different habitat to Nagat1. Short slope from reef crest to sand bottom at 13-15m. Some overhangs and large bommies, but patchy corals, much algae,several SC, Millepora and sand. viz terrible at 8m, due to tide.
Well structured reef slope, about 40 degrees, with good diversity of corals and moderate rugosity. Drops to well over 20m with coral growth but did not dive that deep.
Patchy reef slope off long sandy beach. Several soft corals, in places small scattered coral heads on sandy silty slope. Some banks of Echinoptera.

Deep reef just off Pemba town, upper plateau at around 17-18m, then drops very steeply. Lots of Halimeda on drop off. Galaxea common on the plateau. Moved up the slope to end of reef before sand of scattered corals in 10-12m.

Two coral pinnacles (dive site "Twin peaks") on the edge of a drop off on a sand platform at around 24 m. Drop off 90 degrees and drops out of sight. Pinnacles rise to around 16-17m and have high coral cover and moderate rugosity.

Fringing reef inshore from the wall off Wimbi beach. Lovely coral gardens in patches with patches of vase corals (Turbinaria? or Pachyseris?). Low relief reef ends on sandy and rubble slope of 20 degrees at around 18m. Scattered soft corals, algae and seagrass (Cymodocea – with the long stem) in patches. Sea very rough so viz not good
NE side of deep reef platform at 25-30m. Stunning coral growth at 25-30 m on the edge of the wall before it drops at 90 degrees or so.
NW side of deep reef platform- Plateau at 15-20m with sand, rubble, some corals, edge of plateau at 25m before dropping vertically on wall

N side of outer Pemba bay: Shallow reef slope to about 18m with patchy corals on sand and rubble bottom; beautiful, varied and high coral cover in the shallows –from around 12-6m, with banks of Montipora and Echinopora. These forming spurs in shallows. some wave damage apparent in shallows.
COTs seen and their scars.

Inside Pemba Bay, silty inner reef. Very few small scattered corals below 15m. At around 12-6m large bommies, banks of Porites rus with reasonable numbers of fish. Further up in 3-4m a “field” of medium sized Porites bommies
Back reef or leeward fringing slope on north of Vamizi Island. Inside the Reserve.
leeward fringing slope on north of Vamizi Island, but west of VA1 and outside the Reserve.Reef edge at ~20m dropping to sand at ~30m. very high coral cover at 16-20m.

Leeward fringing slope on north of Vamizi Island. Gentle slope from around 10 to 17m, then drops to >25m but Very strong current so did not go deeper than 19m.Low relief, rubble, lots SC and Millepora.
Leeward fringing slope on north of Vamizi Island, west of VA2, and outside the Reserve. Reef plateau at around 10-15m, slopes to sandy rubble bottom with scattered corals at 20m.

Narrow reef platform off crest of fringing reef near NE point of Vamizi island. Platform at 7-12 m, high relief, but coral cover and diversity not that high. then drops at around 50 degrees to sandy slope at around 20m. Further out this drops to 200m or so. Large bommies, sandy gullies and strong water flow.

Narrow reef platform off crest of fringing reef near NE point of Vamizi island. Platform at 7-12 m, moderate relief, but coral cover and diversity not that high. then drops at around 50 degrees to sandy slope at around 20m -30m. Further out this drops to 200m or so.

Submerged reef plateau at 6-10m on top with channels; walls drop to several hundred metres. Strong currents at times. Aggregates grey reef sharks and snappers (particularly L. gibbus), and at least 1 resident Epinephelus tukula.

Further east and slightly south of VA5 and VA6. 90 degree wall with Turbinaria corals, drops to sand and rubble bottom w vase sponges around 25-30m. Top platform 17-10m w scattered bommies, lots sand & silt, low coral cover. Much more sand and silt flow than at VA5 and VA6.
large amounts of floating algae. fisher said it was normal with rains, we were not sure about this, enver seen it before
shallow reef edge, slight silt, borders SG in places; 1 large COT
small coral heads - Porites, Acropora, rubble, sand alot of SG and some brown algae - Sargassum & Turbinaria
gentle reef slope to 15m, high coral cover, large banks of staghorn . Old 2010 site - Metundo7. WP is Nick Hill's, the 1 infront to distinguish it (ie 463 in his datafile)
gentle reef slope to 15m, high coral cover but low relief, occasional large massives different spp. banks of staghorn . WP is Nick Hill's, the 1 infront to distinguish it (ie 463 in his datafile)
extensive flat plateau at 8-10m off Metundo island, same site as Metundo7 in 2010
same as Metundo NE1 but further east and more exposed and sloping
shallow fringing reef, moderate relief, high live coral, some silt, sand patches, rubble and brown algae further inshore. 3 tn only
Plateau dominated by Acropora plates some dead, 7-13m, then vertical wall with gorgonians
Pinnacle in lagoon w Porites bommies on top in 2-3 m, 50 deg slope, high variety of coral species, very turbid, bottom at 18-20m w much dead coral
Plateau, 7-15m, dominated by many med sized Porites and Acropora plates some dead, medium relief, 70 deg wall to approx 35m with gorgonians
Plateau, 6-13m, lots of dead Acropora plates
Plateau, 4-14m, w many Porites, wall w low relief 80 degree slope to sand and scattered corals at 30-40m
high coral cover and diversity in top 12-15 m, below that dominated by Lobophyllia and some Porites extending across the floor at 16-20m
low relief highly exposed reef slope with upper flat at 6-8m, slope of 45 deg to sand bottom at around 35m. coral colonies abundant, mainly Pocillopora, Styllophors, some Porites
low relief highly exposed reef slope with upper flat at 6-8m, slope of 45 deg to sand bottom at around 35m. coral colonies abundant, mainly Pocillopora, Styllophors, some Porites
100m plateau 3-19m, acrop plates dead/alive, wall dropping steeply with coral growth beyond view
Fringing reef to sand bottom at 12-13m. High coral cover, dominated by several growth forms of Acropora.
Plateau from 3-10m w extensive dead Acropora plates, Halimeda, wall from 10m to 25-30m with some dead plates in upper portion, fans from 16m
Shallow fringing reef only to 7-10m on sand. Spurs and grooves with exceptionally high coral cover all over
Plateau 3-10m, steep wall but coral ends at around 16m.
fringing reef from crest with slope w very high coralcover
large knoll with high plates coralcover on topand on slope, tosand bottom at 16-20m. Was called lagknolls - changed to lagS for chagos paper
large knoll with high Porites coral cover on top and on slope, to sand  at 16m. seabed at 22-23 m w high coralcover. Was called lagknolls - changed to lagS for chagos paper
fringing reef from crest with slope w very high coralcover
Plateau 8-10m w high coral cover, sandy steepwall. LS only
Plateau at 8m, steep wall, a lot of dead coral mainly Acropora plates. Highest live coral on plateau, many small Porites and some medium sized Acropora plates. Steep wall with many dead corals
Plateau at 8m, then 95 degree wall of sand rock and small corals with fans, no bottom in site. Plateau rich with coral cover but also brown algae mats in some areas
plateau 8-11m, then gentle slope to 18-20m giving way to sand. slope w high relief and mod CC, lots plates
wide plateau mainly dead, v low LCC, wall at 23m
wide plateau 10-14m of rock, sand and dead coral, low relief some live Porites. Then short slope from 14-17m to bottom at 20m of sand with scattered coral heads.
high cover dead coral, softs, sand, Halimeda and Millepora common, low relief, slope to 19m sand w many scattered corals
very dead reef plateau 9-16m, low relief, rubble, soft corals, then slopes at 45 deg to >25m, also low reief, little LC
plateau to 9m with many dead plates, some live;  wall edge with most LC. Wall drops to around 25m with caves and fans, coral stops giving way to sandy slope
bare rock plateau, live coral in patches, fans on wall
knoll w large Acropora plates, some Porites bommies, alot dead and heavy silt so viz terrible
bare rock & sand plateau w some LCC, wall at 11m
sandy knoll top,  Acropora plates, coral deeper
Strip of Porites boulders on sand and seagrass in channel
Wide slope starting at around 10m, with gentle spur and groove formation. Very rich live coral growth and diversity; moderate relief.
Wide slope starting at around 12m depth, with gentle spur and groove formation. Rich live coral growth but low relief. Soft corals common.
Narrow fringe of corals in 1-7m depth bordering Kiwe which is a large patch reef that is exposed at low tide. Rubble, sand, some silt and isolated coral heads, some dead some live
Fringe of live coral, medium to high bommies, on sand in 1-3m. Some large Porites and high LC especially in 1-2.5m. Rubble patches, sand and seagrass bordering the fringe of corals.
Shallow strip of largely dead reef bordering seagrass. Large areas of rubble. Several small live Acropora
Reef plateau at 5-7m depth fringing uplifted fossil coral rock edge. Plateau edge about 100m from rocks, slopes at ~ 65o , very high LC to around 22m.
Very wide reef slope at 7-9m, slope at ~10o, low relief, high LC, mainly Acropora plates and some staghorn, some rubble and SC patches
Plateau at 5-7m depth, then drops to 20-22m. Wall fairly bare with sea whips and some small Tubastrea. At 20m high coral cover of Pachyseris extending across a gentle sloping seabed.
Plateau at 7-9m, some spur and groove structure with some sand channels. Some large Acropora plates and large Porites. Medium relief. High LC.
Very shallow (<3m) patch reef, but with high LC dominated by Acropora plates and digitate forms, occasional Porites bommies. Sand very silty,

Very shallow (1-3m) fringe of coral, edging a very large exposed flat at low tide. Seagrass quite common along the edge. Reef largely Acropora, staghorn and much of it alive. One large bank of Galaxea. Very silty sand bottom.

Sheltered inner bay on the north west side of Rongwe Island with scattered coral patches on sand in 0.5-1.5m depth. Large areas of sand, some with scattered rubble. Live Acropora, and a lot of dead stag horn Acropora with filamentous black algae. Halimeda algae also commmon.
South western end of Takamaji Island. Shallow patches of reef on sand bottom and in places rock substrate. Patches dominated by an extensive bank of Porites cylindrica. Some silt.

SE end of Quiwia peninsula. Fore reef, gentle slope ~35degrees. Medium relief but low lying growth forms of corals, boulder forms, very high LC and coral species diversity; some SC. Some sand and rubble channels in <6m depth.
Semi-sheltered reef patches behind the fore reef though facing SE. Large banks  of staghorn Acropora and other Acropora growth forms. Very high LC.  Medium relief. Ends on sand at ~10m.
Very high reef relief in places with massive Porites, and P. rus, Acropora, Favids; plus gentle slope of Goniopora with Halimeda, patches of Fungids and sand. Reef ends at 16-19m depth.

Low relief 20 degree slope with a range of LC species including Acropora plates and small massives. Soft coral common, silty sand and rock bottom in places. A ridge of medium relief at 10-12m. Areas of rubble and sand, some looks like storm damage. Reef ends at 13-14m on sand with scattered rubble.

Reef plateau of northern fore reef slope at 4-5m depth with many sand channels and open sand areas; live coral as massive growth forms and small Acropora, DC and SC common and bare rock. Digitate Porites also common. Then drops at 6m to a slope of rubble and extensive banks of Galaxea which extend to 14-17m depth.

Protected back reef facing west towards Palma. Shallow lagoon like coral garden dominated by large areas of staghorn Acropora, relatively high LC, occasional large Acropora plates and areas of sand in 5-6m. Fire coral also common in large mounds. Large areas of staghorn rubble – looks like storm damage. Rubble in places quite consolidated with CCA.
Offshore deep reef with plateau at 12-17m, then slopes gently to sand, rubble, rock and algae bottom at 21m. Very low rugosity  reef. Occasional sponges, occasional small Millepora, Halimeda common.
Offshore plateau with top at 8-10m. Did not manage to find the slope. Very low rugosity rocky reef with algae, some sand. Encrusting Montipora, some small Acropora heads, sponges.

Inner reef inside Kui bay opposite mlango. Runs parallel to shore – narrow fringe of very high rugosity Porites bommies. And one strip runs towards shore. Many dead bommies, but some live. High silt load, Halimeda common. Seagrass and sand surrounds the strip.

Very narrow fringe of corals inside Kui bay in channel running south near small fossil rock islands. High live coral cover and diversity in patches. High rugosity. Large Porites bommies, some dead. Silt high.

Plateau at ~10m with occasional small Acropora. Slopes at ~30 degrees from 15-20m. Rocky slope with  ledges so moderate rugosity in places – patchy, mostly low rugosity. High cover of Halimeda, some sponges, silty. Bottom at 20m of rock, sand and turf algae.

Shallow fringe of reef outside small fossil coral island off southern end of Kiwaiyu Island. Seagrass surrounds the reef. High coral cover and diversity. Some large Porites bommies, CCA. High rugosity in most places, some flat areas with low coral cover, Turbinaria algae common in patches.Sand and seagrass on deeper side at 5m.
slope to sand at 16m, small massives, high algae & dead coral <5m, v. silty
Ankali Outer: submerged bank, reef slope to >20m. Large Porites & other massives domiante slope, highrelief; + Pocillopora, some large Acrp. Plates & stags. Gentle slope w rich coral growth, some DC.
Ankali Inner: top of bank, shallow, flat bottom massive corals with sand patches, good coral diversity
short slope to sand at 16m; lots DC and silt, <5m all algae & DC

Shallow (1-8m) patch reef on sand with high relief Porites lobata and banks of Pocillopora, + Acropora plates. Large areas of Stypodium algae growing between coral heads, also Dictyota. One long dive for whole site.

Outer reef edge just north of the small town of Obock. Rich coral growth, diversity, medium to high relief, many massives and encrusting corals. Fish abundant, schools of scarids, snapper, Caesio & large sized and varied groupers.

Outer reef edge just north of the small town of Obock. Steep slope, Rich coral growth, diversity, medium to high relief, many massives and encrusting corals; some silt, and Millepora. Fish abundant, schools of scarids, snapper, Caesio & chaetodons.
Coral garden inside lagoon. Some good coral cover and diversity on flat areas of sand, very silty poor viz.
Coral garden inside lagoon. Some good coral cover and diversity on flat areas of sand, very silty poor viz.

Daley: Narrow reef slope fringing the coastline, drops to sand at 5-10m, very silty, visibility 6m. Porites columnar form common, and dominates, some other LC, a lot of DC and a lot of encrusting algae, especially on top of reef at 3-4 m.

Daley: Narrow reef slope fringing the coastline, drops to sand at 5-10m, very silty, visibility 6m. Porites columnar form common, and dominates, some other LC, a lot of DC and a lot of encrusting algae, especially on top of reef at 3-4 m.

Ras Douan:Forereef slope drops from a plateau at 4-6 m, with large massives, mainly Porites, both massive and encrusing. Fairly steep slope with sand patches, lots of dead coral and some rubble; several black corals – whips and fragile Antipatheria fans. Silty. Reef ends on sandy slope at 19-20 m.

Sable Blanc: Forereef slope. A lot of rubble on the shallow plateau at 2-4 m and some encrusting algae and some massives and Acropora. Reed edge at around 7m, then drops quite steeply with large massives, high coral cover, mainly Porites, both massive and encrusing, and drops to sandy slope at 23-25 m where the reef ends. More dead coral at depth. Silty.

Khorambado: narrow fringing reef slope, low-medium relief, dropping to sand at 6-7m. Very turbid, with high levels of suspended sediment. High levels of rubble, dead coral and sand patches. Encrusting brown algae common. Top of reef with high cover of Sargassum. Some live Porites bommies and other small LC heads.

Dorale:Narrow fringing reef slope, low-medium relief,  some algae and sand patches, dropping to sand at 14-15m with scattered coral heads continuing down slope. Top of reef with high cover of Sargassum. Very turbid. Towards the point large Porites heads in 2-5m full of Lutjanus fulviflamma, Kyphosids, very large L. bohar and one Ch. undulatus. Some fishing line, some Antipatheria, some sponges.

Reef slope with high coral cover, mainly Acropora, some very large plates, medium to low relief dropping to sand slope at > 26m.  At depth calcareous algae. Reef formed in spurs with wide sand areas between.

Reef slope with high coral cover, mainly Acropora, some very large plates, encrusting corals, high LC cover, medium relief dropping to sand slope at 45 degrees at around 18m. Reef plateau at 1.5-3 m all hard coral – live (Pocillopora and Porites) or dead.
Narrow fringing reef slope drops to sand at 7-8m. Suspended sediment in water, poor viz (6-7m). High LC at <5m with extensive banks of Pavona, some Galaxea banks. Platax, Kyphosids and Carangids.
Narrow fringing reef slope drops to sand at 7-8m. Suspended sediment in water, poor viz (6-7m). High LC at <5m with extensive banks of Pavona, some Galaxea banks. Platax, Kyphosids and Carangids.
Pt. Gabrielle - Rock and boulder wall with corals, no accretion. Sand at 10m, almost flat with Favids and very small Acropora heads. Large Porites bommies off the wall on sand.

Parrot Island: Rock wall with corals and scattered boulders also with corals; no accretion. Some enormous Acropora plates especially in 3-8m; some dead. Sand bottom with some silt, slopes gently with scattered small coral heads eg Millepora and Acropora.

Steep rock slope, about 75 degrees,  from the “red mountain” with high LC cover in <10m, mainly encrusting on boulders and rock wall and some massive Porites. Corals in spurs with sand inbetween. Reef / rock gives way to sandy slope with isolated coral heads on boulders to > 30m. Plateau at 1-2 m of small coral bommies, lots of Porites.

45 degree slope with rock and some boulders. Live coral high at <8m, high cover of Porites, but some bare rock and dead coral, below that coral heads scattered on a sandy slope which becomes mainly sand at 13-15m.

Narrow reef slope which ends at 11-15 m on sandy slope which continues with occasional large boulders with small coral heads. Some silt. Reef slopes at 45 degrees, medium relief, medium LC, some sand patches. Mainly small Acropora, occasional large plates, mixed species, some bare rock. One end of the site with large boulders little LC, and large E. fuscoguttatus.
Narrow reef slope to sand at 7m. Silty sand with suspended sediment in water column. Viz poor at 7m. Acropora dominated slope at 45 degrees, sand patches, some large Porites bommies in 1-3 m.

Narrow reef slope that ends at 10m on sand slope with occasional coral bommies. Some silt, visibility poor, 8 to 9m. Medium relief reef with medium LC cover:  small Acropora plates, small Porites. Very high LC in < 5m, 90% of which is Porites. Some Turbinaria < 3m.
Narrow reef slope to sand at 12 m. Medium relief dominated by columnar Porites; some DC. Some patches of rubble and algae in <5m. Some silt, visibility poor, 8 to 9m.
